method: Abstract read on DOAJ (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil record) for Haugen 2023; PubMed record 37582807. Schwanbeck 2020 from its PubMed record 32358310 (seed source; not quoted on screen).

claims.claim: A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis found similar muscle growth with machine-based and free-weight training.
claims.source_title: Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims.authors: Haugen ME, Vårvik FT, Larsen S, Haugen AS, van den Tillaar R, Bjørnsen T
claims.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis: 13 studies, 1,016 participants; 5 studies measured hypertrophy
claims.finding: Direct comparison of hypertrophy: no difference between free-weight and machine training (SMD -0.055, 95% CI -0.397 to 0.287, p = 0.751). Strength gains were specific to the modality trained; the authors conclude the choice is down to individual preferences and goals.

claims.claim: Machines guide the movement on a fixed path, which makes them easier to learn (practical statement, not presented as a study finding).
claims.finding: Not attributed to a study in the narration.
